questions.feedback: That trap reading is the one to unlearn: A catalyst pushes the equilibrium toward the products. Reteach point: A catalyst speeds the forward and reverse reactions equally: the position of equilibrium is unchanged.
questions.misconception: A catalyst pushes the equilibrium toward the products.
questions.prompt: A catalyst is added to a reversible reaction already at equilibrium. What changes?

questions.feedback: Count the gas moles: N2 + 3 H2 is 4 moles of gas, 2 NH3 is 2 moles. Raising the pressure shifts the equilibrium to the fewer-moles side, to the right - the second disturbance in scene s5.
questions.prompt: The pressure on the Haber equilibrium N2 + 3 H2 <-> 2 NH3 is raised at constant temperature. What happens, and why?

questions.answer: A dynamic equilibrium is a reversible reaction in a closed system where the forward and reverse rates are equal, so the concentrations stay constant even though both reactions keep running.
questions.feedback: Both halves live in scene s5: the rates are equal and the system is closed - the bars stop moving not because the reactions stop, but because they balance.
